name: Guanajuato
tagline: A silver-mining city of multicoloured houses stacked up a steep valley, with underground streets, tiny plazas, a famous mummy museum and a student-filled, serenade-loving centre.
highlight: The Callejón del Beso and the Pípila viewpoint, at dusk, as the hillside lights come on.
shortDescription: A UNESCO-listed colonial city in a ravine, with baroque churches, winding alleys, underground tunnels, the Diego Rivera birthplace museum and a lively university atmosphere.
metaDescription: A Guanajuato travel guide: the Callejón del Beso, the Pípila viewpoint, Alhóndiga de Granaditas, the Mummy Museum, underground tunnels, Cervantes festival, where to stay and a two-day plan.
knownFor: Colourful hillside houses, alleys, tunnels, the mummy museum, serenades

image.alt: The colourful houses of Guanajuato packed into a hillside valley

intro: Guanajuato sits in a narrow ravine in the Mexican highlands, and it grew rich in the 18th century on silver. At its peak, its mines produced a large share of the world's silver, and the wealth paid for churches, theatres and mansions that still stand. It was also the cradle of the Mexican independence movement: the first major battle of 1810 took place at the Alhóndiga de Granaditas.

The city's oddities come from its geography. Streets are too narrow and steep for cars, so many of the main roads run underground through old mining tunnels. Houses in bright colours climb the hills, and tiny plazas and alleys, such as the Callejón del Beso, where balconies almost touch, fill the centre. UNESCO listed the city and its mines in 1988.

It is also a young city, with a large university. Students in medieval costume lead evening serenades called callejoneadas, cafés and bars are busy, and the annual Cervantino arts festival in October fills the streets with music and theatre.

whyVisit.intro: Guanajuato is one of the most charming and unusual cities in Mexico, and it is compact and easy on foot.

points.title: Colour and shape
points.text: Pastel houses climb steep hillsides in a way that recalls a stage set, and the maze of alleys rewards wandering.

points.title: Underground streets
points.text: Former mine tunnels carry traffic beneath the centre, an unusual sight and a sensible solution.

points.title: A young, musical city
points.text: Students, buskers and callejoneada troupes give the evenings a festive air.

points.title: Historic sites
points.text: The Alhóndiga, Basilica, Teatro Juárez and Universidad de Guanajuato are all within a short walk.

points.title: Quirky museums
points.text: The Museo de las Momias displays naturally mummified bodies, and the Diego Rivera birthplace holds early works.

attractionsIntro: The centre is compact, and two days is enough for the main sights.

attractions.name: The Callejón del Beso

image.alt: The narrow Callejón del Beso in Guanajuato with balconies almost touching

attractions.text: A tiny alley where the balconies of two houses are so close that neighbours could kiss across them, and according to legend two lovers did. It is a local ritual to kiss on the third step.
attractions.tip: Go early to avoid the crowds.

attractions.name: The Pípila monument and viewpoint
attractions.text: A statue of a folk hero of the independence war on a hill above the centre, with a panorama of the city. A funicular runs up from the Teatro Juárez.

attractions.name: The Alhóndiga de Granaditas
attractions.text: A former granary turned fortress, where the first great battle of the independence war took place in 1810. It is now a regional museum with murals by José Chávez Morado.
attractions.tip: Read the plaques for the story.

attractions.name: The Basilica and Plaza de la Paz
attractions.text: A yellow baroque basilica housing the Virgin of Guanajuato, surrounded by mansions and cafés.
attractions.tip: Have a coffee on the plaza.

attractions.name: The Teatro Juárez and Jardín de la Unión
attractions.text: A grand neoclassical theatre with a colonnade and lions, next to the leafy garden that is the city's living room.

attractions.name: The Museo de las Momias
attractions.text: A museum of naturally mummified bodies from the local cemetery, a macabre and famous attraction.
attractions.tip: Not for the squeamish or for small children.

attractions.name: The Diego Rivera Museum
attractions.text: The house where the muralist was born, now a museum with a collection of his early works and family furniture.

thingsToDoIntro: Guanajuato is for slow walking, and for evenings out.

thingsToDo.title: Get lost in the alleys
thingsToDo.text: Follow the stairs and lanes uphill, and stop for coffee in the tiny plazas.

thingsToDo.title: Join a callejoneada
thingsToDo.text: Students in traditional costume lead a singing, drinking, storytelling walk through the alleys at night.
thingsToDo.tip: Book a ticket the same day.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the funicular to Pípila
thingsToDo.text: A short ride with views over the whole city.

thingsToDo.title: Attend the Cervantino festival
thingsToDo.text: A month-long arts festival in October, with performers from around the world.

thingsToDo.title: Visit a silver mine
thingsToDo.text: The Valenciana mine and its church are just outside the centre.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the tunnels
thingsToDo.text: Walk or drive through the underground streets, some of which follow old river beds.

foodIntro: Guanajuato's cooking is central Mexican, with enchiladas mineras, miners' style, as its signature.

foods.name: Enchiladas mineras
foods.text: Tortillas dipped in chile sauce, filled with cheese and served with potatoes, carrots and chicken, the miners' dish.

foods.name: Guacamayas
foods.text: Crusty bolillo rolls stuffed with pork crackling and a hot salsa.

foods.name: Nieves and paletas
foods.text: Sorbets and ice pops of local fruit.

foods.name: Cajeta and sweets
foods.text: Goat's milk caramel and candied fruit, sold in the markets.

foods.name: Tacos and carnitas
foods.text: Simple tacos at busy stands and in the market.

foods.name: Local wine and mezcal
foods.text: Wine from the surrounding vineyards, and small-batch mezcal.

accommodation.intro: Stay in the historic centre, in a restored mansion or guesthouse, to walk everywhere.

areas.name: Centro histórico
areas.text: Boutique hotels and guesthouses near the Jardín de la Unión and the Basilica.

areas.name: The hills
areas.text: Small hotels on the slopes, with views but steep climbs.

gettingThere.intro: Guanajuato is about 350 km north-west of Mexico City.

options.text: About 5 hours from the Terminal Norte, with several daily services.
Flights from Mexico City and US cities, then a 45-minute transfer.

gettingAround.intro: The centre is walkable, and taxis and buses cover the rest.

options.text: Most sights are within a short walk, with steep climbs.
Cheap and plentiful, useful for hilltop sites.
Runs from the Teatro Juárez to Pípila.

bestTime.headline: October–April
bestTime.summary: At 2,000 m, Guanajuato has a mild climate, with a rainy season from June to September.

seasons.text: Dry, sunny and cool in the evening.
Afternoon rain, green hills, fewer visitors.
Pleasant, with the Cervantino festival in October.

bestTime.avoid: The Cervantino weeks if you want quiet, and Semana Santa.

itinerary.title: Two days in Guanajuato
itinerary.intro: The historic sights on the first day, viewpoints and museums on the second.

days.title: The historic centre
days.morning: The Basilica, the Jardín de la Unión and the Teatro Juárez.
days.afternoon: The Callejón del Beso and the Alhóndiga.

days.title: Views and museums
days.morning: The Diego Rivera Museum and the market.
days.afternoon: The Valenciana mine or the Mummy Museum.

tipsIntro: Guanajuato is small and walkable, and a few tips help.
tips: Wear comfortable shoes. The streets are steep and cobbled.
Book a hotel with a central location.
Go early to the Callejón del Beso.
Join a callejoneada for a memorable evening.
Watch for traffic in the tunnels, which are also used by pedestrians.
Book well ahead for the Cervantino festival.
Bring a jacket for the evenings.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Guanajuato?
faq.a: Two days is enough for the sights. Add a day for the mines or a trip to San Miguel de Allende.
The city's tourist centre is generally regarded as safe, though the state has seen violence elsewhere. Check your government's advice and use normal precautions.
A night-time walking musical parade through the alleys, led by students in traditional costume, with songs and stories.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?
faq.a: October to April. The Cervantino festival in October is lively, and busy.

faq.q: Can I visit as a day trip from San Miguel de Allende?
faq.a: Yes, but it is a long day. An overnight stay is better.
Because the ravine is too narrow for roads, engineers built roads in old mine tunnels and river channels to relieve traffic in the 20th century.
